about_page_description: Third-year audio student at DAE Belgium. Piano background, audio for 4 games, and a growing collection of tools I built because the manual way got old.
intro: 22, based in Belgium. Third-year game audio student at DAE. Shipped audio for 4 student games so far.
story_1: Started piano at six. Twelve years of lessons. Somewhere in high school I got more curious about why sound works than how to play it. Switched to math and physics, then started writing Python scripts to fix broken audio files.
story_2: At DAE I built a beatbox classifier because the off-the-shelf ML models couldn't keep up. Wrote Wwise repair scripts because fixing references by hand after every Perforce merge got old fast. Did audio for 4 student games in Wwise, MetaSounds, and FMOD.
story_3: For my thesis I tested whether AI can generate game audio in real-time. Short answer: not yet. But I built a caching system that serves pre-generated sounds in under 55ms, which is fast enough for most gameplay.
pull_quote: If the player can't hear the enemy because the ambient is too loud, that's not a design choice. It's a bug.
approach_1: Most of my work starts with something breaking. Footsteps playing on the wrong surface. A SoundBank eating twice the memory budget. That's when you learn what matters. When four players share one screen and one audio budget, you cut what doesn't need to be there.
approach_2: I build tools when I have to do the same annoying task twice. Wwise kept breaking after pulls, so I wrote a script to fix it. Now the team uses it. Same with the Unreal Engine Rebuilder. If it wastes time, automate it.
cta_text: Looking for a game audio internship in 2026. 3-6 months, EU passport, can relocate.
